title: ChanSFormer: A Channel Agnostic Vision Transformer for Multi-Channel Cell Painting Images
claim: Disentangling attention into channel-wise and spatial steps with per-channel CLS tokens gives a channel-agnostic encoder usable for supervised and self-supervised training.
layout: 4 panels; large framework left, three stacked or side panels right, left-to-right flow
description: A four-panel method figure. Panel (a) on the left shows two microscopy channel images, one cyan and one yellow. Each channel goes through shared patch embedding and a position embedding, drawn as rows of small orange or green token blocks with numbered pink boxes. A single blue learnable CLS token is copied into per-channel CLS tokens with blue arrows. All tokens feed an orange ChanSFormer Encoder × L box, which outputs tokens. Panel (b) shows supervised classification, where channel CLS tokens pass through a blue Attn box to give one image output. Panel (c) shows DINOv2 pretraining with DINO loss on the CLS tokens and iBOT loss on the patch tokens. Panel (d) shows the encoder internals as a vertical stack: channel attention, then spatial attention, then MLP, with red outlines on the attention blocks. Orange and green colors mark the channels throughout.
caption: (a) Overall framework of ChanSFormer. Each channel of an input image is independently projected by a shared patch embedding; a shared spatial positional embedding is added, and individual channel class (CLS) tokens, copied from a single learnable CLS token, are concatenated. The resulting tokens pass through L ChanSFormer encoders. (b) Supervised classification. The channel CLS tokens are aggregated via attention into an image-level representation. (c) Self-supervised DINOv2 pretraining. The channel CLS tokens are treated as distinct samples to generate the DINO loss [ref], while the remaining patch tokens generate the iBOT [ref] loss. (d) Architecture of the ChanSFormer encoder. A single global attention block is replaced by channel attention (across channels, per spatial position) followed by spatial attention (across spatial positions, per channel).
abstract: High-content multi-channel imaging, from Cell Painting assays to remote sensing, is central to modern scientific pipelines. Because these channels are highly heterogeneous and experimental configurations frequently evolve, a practical vision backbone must be fundamentally channel-agnostic. Current channel-adaptive vision transformers rely on global self-attention with learnable channel embeddings, which can be computed only for previously known channels. Attempts to overcome this limitation of new channels either discard the embeddings, losing channel identity, or process each channel independently, thereby eliminating critical cross-channel interactions. To address this, we introduce ChanSFormer, an efficient Vision Transformer that replaces rigid embeddings with disentangled spatial-channel attention and individual channel CLS tokens. This architecture natively preserves both distinct channel identities and cross-channel information flow. Furthermore, the individual channel class token design unlocks more informative feature representations for self-supervised learning and enables representation-based channel sampling while remaining channel-agnostic. We evaluate ChanSFormer on two biology multi-channel datasets, CHAMMI, JUMP-CP and a satellite dataset, So2Sat. Experimental results show that ChanSFormer outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 3.93%-4.27% on JUMP-CP in classification accuracy. It also demonstrates exceptional cross-dataset transferability under a self-supervised setting, outperforming previous methods by up to 2.72% in accuracy in the same classification tasks. Furthermore, the disentangled attention reduces the quadratic complexity of channel-by-spatial sequence length of the global attention baseline, thus improving throughput by 55%-313%. Code is available at https://github.com/cvlab-stonybrook/ChanSFormer.
